classification.difficultyReason: Use inverse trigonometric functions and quadrant reasoning, retaining precision until the final rounding.

content.prompt: Using a calculator, find, correct to two decimal places, the angles $\theta$ between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ inclusive, such that:

answer.worked:
In degree mode, the related angle is $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.2745)\approx15.93221965^\circ$. Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\text{ or }180^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx15.93^\circ\text{ or }164.07^\circ\end{align*}$$

In degree mode, the related angle is $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(0.9165)\approx23.58034688^\circ$. Cosine is negative in quadrants II and III.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-\alpha\text{ or }180^\circ+\alpha\\\theta&\approx156.42^\circ\text{ or }203.58^\circ\end{align*}$$

In degree mode, the related angle is $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(2.2465)\approx66.00439003^\circ$. Tangent is positive in quadrants I and III.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\text{ or }180^\circ+\alpha\\\theta&\approx66.00^\circ\text{ or }246.00^\circ\end{align*}$$

In degree mode, the related angle is $\alpha=\sin^{-1}(0.8976)\approx63.84436950^\circ$. Sine is negative in quadrants III and IV.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ+\alpha\text{ or }360^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx243.84^\circ\text{ or }296.16^\circ\end{align*}$$

In degree mode, the related angle is $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(0.7010)\approx45.49271070^\circ$. Cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=\alpha\text{ or }360^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx45.49^\circ\text{ or }314.51^\circ\end{align*}$$

In degree mode, the related angle is $\alpha=\tan^{-1}(2.5884)\approx68.87650653^\circ$. Tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-\alpha\text{ or }360^\circ-\alpha\\\theta&\approx111.12^\circ\text{ or }291.12^\circ\end{align*}$$
